page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5-c4g1.xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading. The instance includes 30.0 GB of system memory, 40 MB of L3 cache, and bundled local storage consisting of a 472 GB SSD. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline of 3 Gbps. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single dedicated NVIDIA Pascal-architecture P100 GPU equipped with 16 GB of VRAM.

Benchmark data highlights a clear structural distinction between general-purpose host CPU capabilities and GPU-accelerated workloads. Single-core and multi-core CPU execution benchmarks, such as stress-ng and PassMark CPU evaluations, fall into the lower performance percentiles. System memory bandwidth also measures low relative to modern cloud platforms, recording 19.43 GB/sec uncached reads. Conversely, hardware-accelerated LLM prompt processing achieves top-tier results, reaching 9863.53 tokens/sec on 135M models and 316.25 tokens/sec on 7B models, with 7B text generation performing in the top 25% at 42.76 tokens/sec.

The instance exhibits a distinct hardware tradeoff: legacy CPU microarchitecture and modest memory throughput are offset by dedicated graphics processing and integrated local SSD storage. This profile yields strong resource density specifically for accelerated parallel operations rather than compute-heavy CPU tasks. The server is optimized for AI inference on small-to-medium models, GPU-accelerated data processing pipelines, and machine learning model evaluation.
